name: Indexing Checklist
description: This module is a short pre-completion checklist of specific items to verify before marking any indexing task, implementation, or piece of work complete.
content:
This module is a short pre-completion checklist of specific items to verify before marking any indexing task, implementation, or piece of work complete.

CORE GUIDELINES
1. Re-check edge cases relevant to indexing (empty input, boundary values, concurrent access) before calling the task done.
2. When indexing guidance conflicts with a specific user instruction, defer to the user's explicit instruction and note the conflict.
3. Before starting indexing work, confirm the scope and constraints so the approach matches the actual requirement.
4. Keep indexing outputs reproducible: fix seeds, record versions, and avoid hidden non-determinism where it matters.
5. Keep indexing changes scoped to what was asked; avoid unrelated cleanup in the same pass.
6. When multiple indexing strategies are viable, name the trade-off explicitly rather than silently picking one.
7. Measure before optimizing any indexing bottleneck; do not guess at what is slow.
8. Prefer the simplest indexing approach that satisfies the requirement over a more general one that isn't needed yet.
9. State assumptions about indexing explicitly before proceeding, rather than leaving them implicit.
10. Document any non-obvious indexing decision with a short rationale so future readers understand the 'why', not just the 'what'.

COMMON PITFALLS TO AVOID
- Do not treat a single passing example as full verification of indexing correctness.
- Do not silently drop indexing edge cases to make an example look cleaner than the real system.
- Do not apply generic indexing advice without checking it fits the specific context at hand.

CLOSING NOTE
Revisit these indexing guidelines if the task's constraints change significantly during the work.
